question: Why is family planning so important for mothers' health in Nigeria?

options.A: It helps reduce maternal mortality by allowing proper pregnancy spacing.
options.B: It removes the need for routine antenatal care visits.
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of chronic illnesses.
options.D: It guarantees financial stability for large households.

explanation: Spot on! Giving the body enough time to recover between pregnancies protects the mother's health and greatly lowers the risk of complications during childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h1)

question: How does child health directly improve when a family uses effective family planning methods?

options.A: The need for childhood immunizations is drastically reduced.
options.B: Children automatically develop stronger natural immunity to all infections.
options.C: Infants are born with a higher average birth weight without exception.
options.D: Resources can be better shared to prevent malnutrition and infant illness.

explanation: You got it! When births are well-spaced, parents can better invest time, money, and nutrition into each child, keeping them healthier and well-nourished. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h1)

question: Why do large family sizes still hold a lot of cultural importance in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Government policies mandate a minimum number of children per household.
options.B: Modern contraceptives are completely unavailable in rural areas.
options.C: They are viewed as a symbol of wealth and ancestral continuity.
options.D: Traditional healers require large families for spiritual protection.

explanation: Exactly! In many traditional settings, having a large family is celebrated as a sign of prosperity, strength, and keeping the family lineage alive. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h2)

question: In some Nigerian households, men make most of the major decisions. How does this affect family planning?

options.A: Maternal mortality rates instantly drop to zero in rural regions.
options.B: Couples automatically adopt natural methods without needing education.
options.C: Health clinics stop stocking hormonal contraceptive injections.
options.D: Women often cannot access modern contraceptives without partner approval.

explanation: Spot on. Because men often lead household decisions, women who want to use family planning may face hurdles or fear disapproval if their partners aren't included in the conversation. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h2)

question: Which family planning method gives you dual protection against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?
explanation: That's right! Barrier methods like male and female condoms block both sperm and infections, making them the only modern contraceptives that offer dual protection. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h3)

question: A client comes to the clinic asking for a reversible method that lasts for several years without her needing to remember it daily. Which option fits best?

options.A: Periodic calendar rhythm tracking with her partner
options.B: Combined oral contraceptive pills taken every morning
options.C: An intrauterine device inserted into the uterine cavity

explanation: Great choice! Intrauterine devices (IUDs) are long-acting and give continuous protection for years without needing daily action from the client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h3)

question: What does 'informed choice' truly mean in family planning counseling?

options.A: Clients must select the method with the highest efficacy rate.
options.B: Clients make voluntary decisions based on complete and accurate information.
options.C: Clients must follow the cultural preferences of their local community.
options.D: Nurses have the final authority to choose the method for the client.

explanation: Spot on! Informed choice means the client gets clear, unbiased facts so they can freely pick the method that works best for them without any pressure. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h4)

question: Why must a nurse take a detailed medical history before a client starts hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: To find out how many children the client's extended family prefers
options.B: To determine the exact date of the client's future menopause
options.C: To check for underlying conditions that might make certain hormones unsafe
options.D: To calculate the precise financial cost of the clinic visit

explanation: You're right! Conditions like a history of blood clots can make certain hormones unsafe, so checking health history first keeps the client safe. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h4)

question: What is a major reason why clients sometimes stop using modern contraceptives early?

options.A: Sudden nationwide shortages of barrier supplies
options.B: Automatic expiration of contraceptive efficacy after one month
options.C: Anxiety and fear regarding normal physiological side effects
options.D: Mandatory government limits on the duration of use

explanation: Spot on! Many clients stop using a method when they notice minor changes like spotting simply because nobody warned them it's a normal body reaction. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h5)

question: How should you respond as a nurse if a client worries that injectable contraceptives will make her permanently barren?

options.A: Provide empathetic education explaining that fertility returns after discontinuation.
options.B: Dismiss the concern as an unimportant superstition unworthy of discussion.
options.C: Advise the client to switch immediately to permanent surgical sterilization.
options.D: Confirm that temporary infertility is a permanent risk of modern drugs.

explanation: Well done! Patient, warm counseling helps clear up myths by calmly explaining that normal fertility returns once the injection wears off. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to getting contraceptives in Nigeria?

options.A: Geographic distance to the nearest healthcare center
options.B: Stockouts of essential commodities at health facilities
options.D: Universal availability of free home-delivery services

explanation: Correct! Free home delivery is not a standard reality across Nigeria. Instead, long distances, running out of supplies, and unfriendly attitudes are the real challenges clients face. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h6)

question: What is the main goal of task-shifting policies in Nigerian family planning programs?

options.A: To restrict contraceptive distribution only to senior medical doctors
options.B: To eliminate the need for any documentation during client visits
options.C: To allow lower-level health workers to provide certain contraceptive services
options.D: To transfer all maternal care responsibilities exclusively to private hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Task-shifting helps bridge the gap by training community health workers and nurses to safely provide methods like injectables where doctors are few. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h6)

question: What is one of the primary clinical duties of a nurse in a family planning clinic?

options.A: Enforcing mandatory family size limits on couples
options.B: Manufacturing pharmaceutical hormone supplies for national distribution
options.C: Assessing clients and administering chosen contraceptive methods
options.D: Conducting major abdominal surgeries for all clients

explanation: You got it! Nurses play a key role by counseling clients, doing health assessments, and giving out chosen methods right there at the primary healthcare level. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h7)

question: Why is community outreach by nurses and midwives so vital for family planning programs?

options.A: It helps engage local leaders and dismantle cultural stigma against modern methods.
options.B: It allows health workers to bypass government health policies entirely.
options.C: It ensures that nurses can collect financial levies from local households.
options.D: It replaces the need for clinical examinations inside health facilities.

explanation: Spot on! Going out into the community builds trust, involves local leaders, and helps clear up cultural or religious worries right at the grassroots level. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h7)
